summary:
I built a single-page app called "Clearwater" with a purple and white theme. `pnpm build` passes. I did not run lint, and I did not open the page in a browser to click through it.

- **Landing page:** the hero staggers in, with slowly drifting purple blobs behind it and a bobbing scroll arrow. Sections fade in as you scroll.
- **Minerals:** tabs switch between four water types (Natural Spring, Rich Mineral, Purified, Alkaline). Each shows total dissolved solids, pH and animated bars for six minerals. Cards beside it explain what each mineral does.
- **How a bottle is made:** five steps from plastic pellets to inspection. Tap a step to expand more detail.
- **Bottling and distribution:** six steps from the water source to the shop, also tap-to-expand.
- **Dark/light switch:** a button in the header toggles the mode. Your choice is saved in the browser and applied before the page paints, so it doesn't flash.

The mineral values are made-up illustrative figures, not taken from any real brand. All content is static.

The README explains how to install and build the app. The page itself is in `src/components/home.tsx`.

Build the prototype for these requirements:

{
  "summary": "An application that shows people information about water bottles. It covers which minerals a bottle of water contains, how a water bottle is made, and more generally how water is bottled and distributed, so that users can find everything they need to know about the subject in one place. The app uses a purple and white colour theme, lets users switch between dark mode and light mode, and has a landing page with smooth animations. No further details about users, workflows or platform were given.",
  "intent": "Build an application that displays information about water bottles, including their mineral content, how they are made, and how water is bottled and distributed, with a purple and white theme, a dark/light mode switch and a landing page with smooth animations.",
  "functional_requirements": [
    "The system must display information about which minerals are in a water bottle.",
    "The system must display information about how a water bottle is made.",
    "The system must display information about how water is bottled and distributed.",
    "The system must use a purple and white visual theme.",
    "The system must provide a switch that lets the user toggle between dark mode and light mode.",
    "The system must display a landing page that uses smooth animations."
  ],
  "user_stories": [
    "As a curious person, I want to see which minerals are in a water bottle so that I know what I am drinking.",
    "As a curious person, I want to learn how a water bottle is made so that I understand how the product is produced.",
    "As a curious person, I want to learn how water is bottled and distributed so that I understand the full journey from source to consumer.",
    "As a user, I want the app to have a purple and white theme so that it looks the way I envisioned.",
    "As a user, I want to switch between dark mode and light mode so that I can view the app in the display setting that suits me.",
    "As a visitor, I want the landing page to have smooth animations so that my first impression of the app is polished and engaging."
  ]
}

I'm sketching out a single-page layout with a hero, an interactive minerals section, step tabs for how it's made, and a distribution timeline. For the theme toggle, I'm leaning toward a small client component that reads localStorage in an effect, with suppressHydrationWarning on the layout to avoid mismatches. Next I'm going to update the theme tokens with some sed-style edits.

I'm going to skip editing the theme tokens line by line and instead append override CSS at the end of the file, since later rules in :root win at equal specificity. After that I'll write one client component for the page content and a separate theme toggle.

I built a single-page app called "Clearwater" with a purple and white theme. `pnpm build` passes. I did not run lint, and I did not open the page in a browser to click through it.

- **Landing page:** the hero staggers in, with slowly drifting purple blobs behind it and a bobbing scroll arrow. Sections fade in as you scroll.
- **Minerals:** tabs switch between four water types (Natural Spring, Rich Mineral, Purified, Alkaline). Each shows total dissolved solids, pH and animated bars for six minerals. Cards beside it explain what each mineral does.
- **How a bottle is made:** five steps from plastic pellets to inspection. Tap a step to expand more detail.
- **Bottling and distribution:** six steps from the water source to the shop, also tap-to-expand.
- **Dark/light switch:** a button in the header toggles the mode. Your choice is saved in the browser and applied before the page paints, so it doesn't flash.

The mineral values are made-up illustrative figures, not taken from any real brand. All content is static.

The README explains how to install and build the app. The page itself is in `src/components/home.tsx`.
